evidence_items.explanation: OpenAI acknowledged unreliable answers at launch. This supports the claim that the problem was publicly knowable from the beginning.

The February–June experiment found a 19% slowdown with AI assistance. Its factor analysis identifies unreliable generations and time spent reviewing or rejecting them as contributors, although the reliability mechanism itself was not separately randomized.

evidence_items.locator: General GenAI Tools: Baseline Functionality, Modest Impact
evidence_items.explanation: The late-2024 survey of 300 US professionals connects modest benefits with rework and identifies unreliable outputs as a challenge for 30% of general-tool users. It also identifies privacy, customization and training barriers, limiting any claim that technical reliability alone explains adoption.

unresolved_gaps: These studies do not estimate how much unreliability explains economy-wide adoption or returns.
The deployment experiment establishes the effect of AI access, while its explanation of the reliability mechanism is observational.
